title: Geo-aware rate limits and currency-aware overage billing: PRD & acceptance criteria
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Problem statement: Enterprise customers operating across APAC, EMEA, and NA require per-region rate limits and quotas that align with regional pricing and local currency billing. Current single-global quota + single-currency overage model causes surprising invoices, misattributed throttles, and poor UX when usage spikes in a single geography. This PRD defines requirements for geo-aware quota policies, currency-aware overage calculation, grace windows, and the acceptance criteria for the billing and console behavior.

Objectives: Provide predictable throttling and billing by region, enable per-region soft-burst behavior, surface clear console billing estimations per currency, and ensure fallbacks to centralized capacity with transparent billing adjustments. Support migration path from global-only quotas with minimum disruption.
scope_included:
- Per-region (region tag = AWS region / cloud region) quotas and rate limits for API + embeddings
- Currency conversion for overage when customer billing currency differs from region currency
- Soft-burst grace windows and automated credit consumption ordering
- UI/Console: per-region quota view, projected overage estimate in customer currency
- Billing: line-item per-region usage, converted overage amount, invoice note describing conversion rate & time
- Rollout strategy: opt-in beta for existing accounts, default for new accounts
scope_out_of_scope:
- Per-zone (AZ) quotas
- Per-model per-region negotiated pricing (separate sales contract work)
- Complex revenue recognition changes outside current invoicing pipelines
requirements: R1: Admins can set region-level soft quotas (monthly units) and hard rate limits (requests/sec) per API key or org
R2: System tracks usage at region granularity and attributes tokens/credits to region buckets first
R3: When billing currency != region default currency, overage is calculated using daily FX midpoint (source: configured FX provider) and recorded on invoice with conversion metadata
R4: Soft-burst grace window configurable (default 6 hours) where overage is charged to temporary burst credit before invoice overage applies
R5: Console shows projected overage in customer currency with the FX rate and a link to historical FX table used for calculation

R6: Fallback routing: if region capacity exhausted, requests can be routed to a compatible model in another region when policy permits; billing must record original region usage and note fallback on invoice
R7: Migration: existing global quota customers can opt into per-region split with an automatic allocation algorithm (based on trailing 90-day regional traffic) and manual override
R8: Audit logs include region decision, currency conversion rate and IDs required for support investigations
R9: Alerting: billing anomalies generated if region-level overage > 3x typical daily burn rate
R10: API: new query params to request region preference; server must validate against customer entitlements
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Create a staging org, set per-region quotas and limits; simulate region-specific traffic and verify throttling occurs only for that region according to configured thresholds

AC2: For an org billed in EUR but using APAC region priced in USD, produce an overage invoice line where USD is converted to EUR using FX provider rate for the invoice date and include conversion metadata in invoice JSON
AC3: Soft-burst behavior: when region usage exceeds soft quota, system uses burst credit for up to configured window; verify burst credit consumption order and a console timeline visual for the event
AC4: Fallback routing: when a region is out-of-capacity and policy allows fallback, requests succeed from fallback region and billing shows original region as primary consumption with a fallback tag
AC5: Console displays per-region projected month-end overage estimate in customer currency with clear disclosure of FX rate and last-sync timestamp

AC6: Migration path: run allocation algorithm for a sample enterprise with 90-day regional distribution and validate resulting bucket allocations; manual overrides persist and do not re-run without admin action
AC7: Auditability: support engineer can retrieve audit log for a given invoice line containing region decision, FX rate ID, and routing fallback ID
AC8: Automated tests: end-to-end test suite reproduces a multi-region spike and validates correct per-region accounting, invoice line items, and console projections
AC9: Performance: per-request region attribution and currency lookup latency added to critical path must be < 5ms p95 in production config
AC10: Documentation: PRD, public support KB, and console tooltips exist and link to the FX provider SLA and the algorithm description
tradeoffs_and_considerations:
- Complexity: regional quotas and FX add billing complexity and invoice length; tradeoff vs. customer predictability.
- Accuracy vs. latency: pulling FX rates in real-time increases latency; we use cached daily midpoint to balance.
- UX: exposing too much billing detail may confuse customers; default views should summarize and provide drilldowns.
- Sales complexity: negotiated per-region pricing remains out of scope for initial rollout.
- Edge cases: region re-mapping (when Redwood renames regions) must preserve historical mapping on invoices.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (Beta): opt-in for select enterprise customers, region-level tracking + console projections + invoice metadata in test sandbox. Phase 2: enable per-region limits for new accounts by default; provide migration tool for existing accounts. Phase 3: GA with billing export and alerts integrated into Console Ops dashboards.
implementation_notes:
- Engineering needs a new region_usage table with denormalized daily aggregates.
- Billing team to extend invoice schema with currency_conversion metadata and fallback_tag.
- Console: new per-region panel and API endpoints for projection.
- Security: FX provider credentials stored in KMS; access audited.
- Legal: include clause about FX timing and customer acceptance in TOS addendum.
open_questions: Q1: Default region currency mapping source — should it be billing account country or region's native currency?
Q2: FX provider: which provider to use in initial rollout and what SLA is acceptable?
Q3: Should soft-burst credits be pooled across regions for enterprises with consolidated billing?
Q4: Are there regulatory constraints for showing FX conversion details in EU invoices?
